reachable: Yes, and with a large measured effect on the training diet — the mechanism is not weak, it points the wrong way. The batcher influences the scored read only through training: which sequences are drawn, and therefore which in-batch negatives the listwise objective couples. Both consumption paths are live. Mechanism 1 (inverse-CDF draw from the raking weights) runs at every step including step 1, and is the whole batch until the block ramp starts. Mechanism 2 (round-robin over fm classes inside blocks) is live once blocks ramp in, covering 75% of each batch from step ~1200 of 4000. On the real 2560-sequence split the composition change is large: pooled h_first accuracy of drawn sequences moves from 0.606 (parent) to 0.344 (candidate), and in the eligible depth-3/4 x 2-mover cell from 0.497 to 0.220. Depth tilt survives (drawn mean depth 3.93 -> 3.895). No dead-parameter question arises: the axis has no parameters, only a sampler.
solves_outside_model: No — nothing is computed for the model. The module resolves mv chains in Python and returns a list of Python ints and nothing else; evolve/harness.py:_train uses those ints only to index fit_stripped and hands the unmodified seq dicts to stream.collate. I verified non-mutation empirically rather than by reading: snapshotted image / cmds / z_cmd / z_obs for 300 sequences, ran 50 batches, and compared — bit-identical. It also owns private torch.Generators (g, g_setup); the global RNG stream is unchanged after 20 batches (checked by reseeding and comparing draws). The z_cmd/z_obs reads in _collision_pools are detached, read-only, and used only to group sequences. So this is sample selection, the legitimate use, and it is not the r-stream retraction shape. One adjacent caution the parent should carry, though: the selection installs an inverted h_first correlation in the diet (see divergence 2), and an anti-first-mover rule is still a role-swap-following analytic non-tracker. If this candidate scores positive, the score may be the frozen slice's realization of that installed cue rather than routing. That is checkable at score time — the adapter already reports `shortcut_leaning` per analytic arm, h_first among them (eval/adapter.py:259, evolve/cups_ca.py:69-129).
summary: The code faithfully implements the algorithm the hypothesis describes; what it does not do is have the effect the hypothesis claims, on the real training data. Everything mechanical checks out: cue_a is exactly the probe's h_first condition (fm_rank==0 agrees with the true h_first hit on 24/24 jail trajectories and 2463/2560 real ones), cue_b is exactly the routed slot's index in the window's expose_order (24/24), the backward walk recovers the scored cups read and its stamped depth (24/24 jail, 2375/2560 real with depth agreeing on all of those), _dbin's stratum 1 is precisely the eligible depth-3/4 slice, raking preserves each stratum's mass exactly, blocks are the pooled union of n_block_images distinct systems drawn without replacement as the crossover partner does it, block weights are wcue x exp(alpha*z), and the round-robin with step rotation and remainder handling is correct. Every mechanical contract claim reproduces: exactly bs in-range ints at steps 1/10/500/4000, bit-identical across same-seed constructions, different across seeds, global torch RNG untouched, fit unmutated, and clean degradation at n=1, n=2, bs=1, one image, no cmds, no mv, hard_frac_max=0, cue_gamma=0. The problem is the premise. The author measured the first-mover cue on 24 jail trajectories and got 54%, comparing it to an assumed chance of ~30% from "2..5 contenders". I ran their own nominated falsifier on the full 2560-sequence training split, which they had no access to: boards have 2 movers on 82% of windows and 3 on the rest, and the cue is at chance conditional on the mover count — 0.494 with 2 movers, 0.501 in the eligible depth-3/4 x 2-mover cell, 0.304 with 3 movers. There is no first-mover shortcut on the real diet to remove. Worse, the estimator has no term for the mover count: it drives the marginal over three rank classes to 1/3 regardless, so where the true null is 1/2 it overshoots and manufactures an inverted cue. Simulated over 4000 steps on the real split, the candidate's diet has h_first accuracy 0.220 in the 2-mover depth-3/4 cell (27% of its draws) against the parent's 0.497 and the population's 0.501 — "the answer is the mover that did not move first" becomes a 78%-accurate rule where nothing exploitable existed before, with an edge over chance roughly 140x the one the hypothesis set out to remove. The author's failure-mode list anticipates the flat-distribution case but predicts a benign no-op ("the raking weights collapse toward 1"); that prediction does not hold, and the shape of the resulting cue is exactly what the objective is built to be suspicious of. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: the score itself — no GPU, no encoded blend root beyond the local cups pack, so I ran no training and no comp_ca. My real-split simulation uses real command strings and real image labels but randomized embeddings, so collision-neighbourhood membership is random rather than embedding-driven; that affects which sequences share a block, not the rank marginals I measured, and the weights-only path (no blocks at all) shows the same inversion. I could not reproduce the author's own simulation numbers for the parent (0.534/0.293/0.173 pooled fm shares — I get 0.438/0.292/0.270) or their "late-phase depth>=4 rises 0.33 to 0.50" (I get 0.72-0.79), because the replication and image-assignment scheme is unspecified; their candidate-side pooled numbers do reproduce closely. Speed claims are untested on the scoring box.

divergences.claim: "'answer = the content whose origin moved first on this board' is right about 54% of the time while the number of contenders on a board is 2..5 (chance roughly 30%)" — the empirical premise the whole mechanism rests on.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The cue the code extracts is real and correctly extracted, but on the FULL real training split it is at chance. Boards have exactly 2 movers on 82% of windows and 3 on 18% — never 4 or 5. Conditional on the mover count (the elimination the probe's `elim` arm shows is textually available), the first-mover rule is right 0.494 with 2 movers and 0.304 with 3 movers, against chance of 0.500 and 0.333. In the eligible depth-3/4 x 2-mover cell it is 0.501. The 54%-vs-30% figure is an artifact of the 24-trajectory jail sample plus an assumption of 2..5 uniformly distributed contenders that the data does not have.
divergences.evidence: Streamed all 2560 sequences of /Users/fanzhu/PyCharmProjects/terminal-wm/data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl, computing h_first from each scored window's own metadata (cups_expose slots + cups_mv steps + routed_idx), i.e. the same quantity evolve/cups_probe.py line 92 computes. Population h_first accuracy: all 0.459; movers=2 (n=2093) 0.494; movers=2 & stamped depth in {3,4} (n=851) 0.501; movers=3 (n=467) 0.304. This is exactly the falsification test the hypothesis nominates ("Falsifiable directly: print the fm_rank/orank histograms over the full fit") and the author could not run it — only the 24 jail trajectories were available to them, where fm_rank is 13/7/4 as claimed (reproduced exactly).

divergences.claim: "The batcher reweights the sequence distribution to destroy exactly those two correlations"; "Flattening fm_rank to ~1/3 inside each depth stratum makes the first-mover rule worth about what guessing is worth"; "The only remaining way to reduce the listwise loss on a routed read is to route."
divergences.what_the_code_does: On the real training split it does the opposite of destroying the correlation: it installs a strong INVERTED one. Because the raking targets a uniform marginal over the three rank classes {0, 1, >=2} rather than the movers-conditional null (0.5 when there are 2 movers, which is 82% of windows), driving the class marginal to 1/3 pushes the first-mover rule below chance. Measured on the real split, the drawn training diet's h_first accuracy in the 2-mover x depth-3/4 cell (27% of the candidate's diet) is 0.220, against 0.497 for the parent and 0.501 in the population. Pooled over all draws it is 0.344 vs the parent's 0.606. So "the answer is the mover that did NOT move first" is right 78% of the time in the slice-matched cell — a cheaper and far stronger order cue (edge 0.28 over chance) than the one the hypothesis set out to remove (edge 0.001). The author's listed failure mode #1 predicts a benign no-op in this situation ("the raking weights collapse toward 1 and this becomes the parent with pooled image blocks"); that prediction is wrong, because the estimator has no term for the mover count.
divergences.evidence: Built a fit from all 2560 real sequences (real cmds, real image labels, randomized embeddings — embeddings only affect collision-pool membership, not the rank marginals) and ran 4000 steps of the parent and the candidate at bs=64, tallying ground-truth h_first hits of every drawn sequence. Candidate: all 0.344, movers=2 0.377, movers=2 & depth3-4 0.220 (share of diet 0.272). Parent: all 0.606, movers=2 0.642, movers=2 & depth3-4 0.497 (share 0.198). Weights alone (no blocks) give 0.354 in that cell, so both consumption paths push the same wrong way.

divergences.claim: "Flattening fm_rank to ~1/3 inside each depth stratum" — the raking weights are described as doing the flattening, with the block round-robin as reinforcement.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The weights alone reach only ~0.43 in the depth-3/4 stratum (from 0.556 in the population) on the jail sample. Two reasons, both in _cue_weights: the 4 IPF sweeps end on the orank axis, so orank comes out exactly uniform and fm_rank — the axis the hypothesis is entirely about — is the one left un-converged (0.401 after 4 sweeps, 0.340 after 50); and the clamp to [1/cue_cap, cue_cap] is applied once AFTER raking rather than inside the loop, undoing part of what was achieved (0.401 -> 0.427). The near-1/3 pooled numbers the hypothesis quotes come mostly from the block-level round-robin, which is a different mechanism than the sentence claims.
divergences.evidence: Ran _rake / _cue_weights directly on the 24 real trajectories per stratum. Stratum depth3-4: population fm 0.556/0.222/0.222; 4 IPF sweeps no clamp 0.401/0.327/0.272; 50 sweeps 0.340/0.333/0.327; impl as configured (cap 4, 4 sweeps) 0.427/0.313/0.260. orank is exactly 0.333/0.333/0.333 after raking in every stratum, before the clamp.

divergences.claim: "raking INSIDE hop-count strata, so the depth marginal is preserved exactly and only the within-depth order correlation is removed" (the stated mitigation for destroying depth information).
divergences.what_the_code_does: True of the raking weights — verified exactly: each stratum's weight share equals its count share to three decimals, because the last operation per stratum is a mean-normalization. Not true of the sampler as a whole: balanced_pick deals block slots round-robin across fm classes with no depth stratification, and fm class correlates with depth, so the drawn depth distribution does shift relative to the parent. The shift is small (drawn mean depth 3.93 parent vs 3.895 candidate) but the late-phase depth>=4 share moves 0.786 -> 0.717 in my replication.
divergences.evidence: Per-stratum weight-share vs count-share printout on a 600-sequence replicated fit (0.500/0.500, 0.375/0.375, 0.125/0.125). Drawn depth histograms over 4000 steps for both impls.

divergences.claim: "the cue is by far the cheapest descent direction available early... gradient descent takes it first" — the argument is specifically about early training, and mechanism 2 is justified by "per-batch balance matters here because the objective's loss is an in-batch listwise softmax".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Only mechanism 1 (the inverse-CDF base draw) is live at step 1, exactly as claimed. Mechanism 2, the per-batch round-robin, lives inside blocks, whose fraction ramps 0 -> 0.75 over the first 30% of steps — so the per-batch balance the argument leans on is absent precisely during the early phase the argument is about. The in-batch-listwise premise itself checks out (r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives builds an n x n target-target ring over all cmd-position rows in the batch).
divergences.evidence: next_batch computes n_hard = round(bs * hard_frac_max * ramp) with ramp = step/(0.3*total_steps); at step 1 of 4000 n_hard is 0, so the whole batch is base_draw. Measured per-batch class counts at steps <=100: 24.3/22.7/16.9 of 64; late (>3500): 22.5/23.9/17.6.

divergences.claim: "orank is 0 in 9, 1 in 10, >=2 in 5" on the 24 jail trajectories; "cue_cap=4.0 bounds the weight ratio".
divergences.what_the_code_does: orank on the 24 is 9 / 9 / 6, not 9 / 10 / 5. And the clamp is followed by a mean renormalization, so individual weights can land just outside [1/cap, cap] — measured min 0.236 against a floor of 0.25. The realized range the hypothesis reports, [0.24, 3.03] with mean 1, reproduces exactly, so this is a wording imprecision rather than an unreported behavior.
divergences.evidence: _scan_seq over the 24 jail trajectories: orank Counter({0: 9, 1: 9, 2: 3, 3: 2, 4: 1}). _cue_weights on the replicated fit: min 0.2361, max 3.0268, mean 1.0.
